c01s03.title: Define the observation
items: Tool placed in its marked location
c01s03.caption: A precise definition makes competing explanations easier to test.

c01s04.title: Reliable and useful differ
c01s04.caption: A consistently counted event can still be the wrong outcome.

c01s05.title: A fair behavioural question
c01s05.caption: Observation and explanation are separate steps.

c02s03.title: A simplified predictive sequence
c02s03.caption: The sequence illustrates a possible learning relation.

c02s03b.title: Two elements in the example
c02s03b.caption: The elements must be defined rather than inferred from a vague story.

c02s04.title: Temporal closeness and information
c02s04.caption: Pairing and predictive value are related but distinct.

c02s05.title: A conditioning claim needs detail
c02s05.caption: A plausible pairing is not yet a causal demonstration.

c03s03.title: An operant question
c03s03.caption: A consequence is classified by its function under the stated conditions.

c03s04.title: Decreasing an action
c03s04.caption: The classification describes a relation; it does not justify using it.

c03s05.title: Classify by relation and effect
c03s05.caption: A correct technical label does not authorize an intervention.

c04s03.title: A possible skill sequence
c04s03.caption: The criteria should track reasoning, not superficial fluency.

c04s03b.title: Teach, then check independence
items: Use a new case without prompts
c04s03b.caption: A practiced chain and transferable understanding need separate checks.

c04s04.title: Different problems need different support
c04s04.caption: Do not infer a learning deficit from a constrained performance.

c04s05.title: Evaluate a skill-building plan
c04s05.caption: A proxy should not replace the intended capability.

c05s03.title: Two arrangements
c05s03.caption: The rule must be distinguished from the observed behavioural effect.

c05s03b.title: Count and time differ
c05s03b.caption: Timing a reward is not automatically an interval schedule unless the response relation is specified.

c05s04.title: Interpret an outcome
c05s04.caption: Controlled schedule effects need contextual interpretation in everyday life.

c05s05.title: A schedule claim needs context
c05s05.caption: A laboratory relation is not an exact forecast for every person.

c06s03.title: Before and during extinction
c06s03.caption: A decrease does not uniquely demonstrate erasure of prior learning.

c06s03b.title: Different return conditions
c06s03b.caption: These are research distinctions, not diagnoses from everyday setbacks.

c06s04.title: Evaluate durable change
c06s04.caption: A return of responding is information about conditions, not moral failure.

c06s05.title: A response-return interpretation
c06s05.caption: Response return calls for explanation rather than blame.

c07s03.title: Training and new cues
c07s03.caption: Transfer must be observed under the actual new conditions.

c07s03b.title: Investigate the controlling condition
c07s03b.caption: A salient difference is a hypothesis rather than an established cause.

c07s04.title: A useful transfer set
c07s04.caption: Transfer involves selecting when a learned relation is relevant.

c07s05.title: Test transfer rather than assume it
c07s05.caption: A well-learned rule includes its limits.

c08s03.title: Not the same outcome
c08s03.caption: An exact movement match is not the only indication of learning.

c08s03b.title: From demonstration to evidence
items: Try a new case with feedback
c08s03b.caption: Performance checks should match the intended learning.

c08s04.title: Interpret observed success
c08s04.caption: Confidence and actual skill require separate checks.

c08s05.title: A demonstration needs a learning check
c08s05.caption: Watching and learning are related but not equivalent.

c09s03.title: A possible habit pathway
items: Action can recur with less thought
c09s03.caption: The model describes a possibility, not a fixed timetable.

c09s03b.title: A small self-directed plan
c09s03b.caption: The plan needs an accessible action and meaningful feedback.

c09s04.title: Evaluate a routine fairly
items: Does it serve the chosen goal?
Does it persist in relevant settings?
c09s04.caption: A useful routine is not established by a universal day count.

c09s05.title: A habit claim needs specifics
c09s05.caption: A cue-linked account is testable without blaming the person.

c10s03b.title: Evaluate more than the count
c10s03b.caption: Technical effectiveness does not settle acceptability.

c10s04.title: A responsible plan
c10s04.caption: Behavioural science should improve options rather than remove them.

c10s05.title: A final behavioural evaluation
c10s05.caption: Effectiveness, inference and ethics require separate attention.
